rounds.text: Mukta Arts Ltd trades at an exceptionally deep discount to its asset backing, with a price-to-book ratio of just 0.63x against a book value of ₹ 89.2 per share [E2], and a P/B of 0.62x compared to a sector benchmark of 6.71x [E7]. The business demonstrates sound financial management through conservative debt positioning, evidenced by a debt-to-equity ratio of 0.30x and a reduction in borrowings to ₹ 59.45 Cr [E38, E39], alongside capital expenditure completion signalled by a 98.4% drop in capital work-in-progress to ₹ 0.13 Cr [E40]. Furthermore, fundamental momentum is turning positive as captured by screens highlighting 73% YoY sales growth, 17% YoY net profit growth, and sequential profit improvement [E67, E69, E70], supported by a healthy free cash flow of ₹ 4.70 Cr [E36]. Conceded: compounded sales growth has contracted over multi-year periods [E14, E15, E16], and the DCF model calculates a negative margin of safety [E44, E45].

The bull highlights a deep asset discount via a price-to-book ratio of 0.63x [E2], but this metric masks severe structural deterioration, including a multi-year compounded sales contraction of 13% over 10 years and 27% over the trailing twelve months [E14, E17]. Conceded: the debt-to-equity ratio sits at a conservative 0.30x and borrowings dropped to ₹ 59.45 Cr [E38, E39], but this leverage is deployed into an underlying business suffering from an operating margin collapse of 28 percentage points down to -9% by Mar 2026 [E30]. While the bull points to completed capital expenditure via a drop in CWIP [E40], earnings quality is heavily compromised by the inclusion of ₹ 15.9 Cr in other income [E64] and alarmingly high debtor days reaching 1,030 days [E65]. Furthermore, the cited short-term profit metrics [E69, E70] fail to offset a miserable median return on equity of just 4% over the last decade [E26], a cash conversion ratio of 0.31x where reported profits vastly outstrip operating cash flow [E34], and a discounted cash flow intrinsic value of ₹ 28 yielding a severe -104.8% margin of safety against the current market price [E44, E45].
